以下はある英語ニュースpodcast記事のFull Story・Point One・Point Twoです。
Point One・Point Twoそれぞれについて、以下6項目を判定してください
(それぞれPASS/FAIL)。

- qa_not_caveat_only: このPointが、研究上の限界・一般化上の注意・免責事項
  だけで構成されていない場合PASS(それらに加えて実質的な新しい内容がある
  場合もPASS。留保だけでPoint枠全体が終わっている場合はFAIL)
- qa_not_full_story_paraphrase: Full Storyの要約・言い換えに留まっていない
  場合PASS(Full Storyの中心的なlogic・結論を語彙だけ変えて繰り返している
  場合はFAIL)
- qa_not_other_point_paraphrase: もう一方のPointの要約・言い換えになって
  いない場合PASS
- qa_explains_why_it_matters: 「だから何なのか」を具体的に説明できている
  場合PASS(聞き手にとっての具体的な意味・示唆がある場合)
- qa_specific_not_generic: この記事のLedger固有の内容に基づいており、他の
  どんな記事にもほぼそのまま流用できる一般論になっていない場合PASS
- qa_adds_new_value: 新しい理解・解釈・意外性・具体的示唆のいずれかを
  実際に加えている場合PASS(Full Storyだけを聞いた場合と比べて、聞き手の
  理解が実際に深まっている場合)

reasoningには、判定理由を1〜2文の日本語で書いてください(特にFAILの場合は
具体的な理由を明記してください)。

【Full Story】
On August 16, 2026, Hanshin quickly made its message clear at Mazda Stadium.

In the first inning, Teruaki Sato hit a two-run home run to center field. Hanshin led 2-0 before Hiroshima could settle in. But an early lead is only the beginning. The real question was whether it would last.

Rihito Ihara gave that lead a steady base. The starting pitcher worked five innings, allowed only two hits, and gave up one run. Hiroshima’s only run came in the fifth, when Elehuris Montero hit a solo home run.

Hiroshima had a chance to make the game closer, but the score did not become a larger exchange of runs. Hanshin stayed in front, then added more in the seventh and eighth innings.

That changed the feeling of the game. The opening home run created the lead. The later scoring made it much harder for Hiroshima to answer.

When the final out arrived, Hanshin had eight runs and Hiroshima had one.

Final score:

Hiroshima 1–8 Hanshin

It was a one-sided win built from an early strike and a lead that kept growing.

【Point One】
Hanshin’s offense is easy to miss if we focus only on Sato. Seishiro Sakamoto drove in a run in the seventh and another in the eighth, while pinch-hitter Fushimi delivered an RBI in the seventh. The lead was built in two stages: an opening blow, then help from the lineup and the bench.

【Point Two】
The pitching story also needs a precise boundary. Ihara’s five-inning start is confirmed, but the available facts do not separately describe the pitchers who followed him. So the safest takeaway is narrower than saying Hiroshima was shut down all night: Ihara gave the early lead a stable foundation.
